name: Punniyakodiyappar Temple, Tiruvidaivasal
deity: Shiva as Punniyakodiyappar (Idaivainathar), with the goddess Abirami
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tiruvidaivasal, near Koradacheri in the Tiruvarur delta, honours Shiva as Punniyakodiyappar with the goddess Abirami. Its Tevaram hymn, long lost, was recovered in 1917 — and with its finding the count of the Paadal Petra Sthalams was completed at 275. A quiet shrine hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar, it keeps a special place in the roll of the Tevaram temples.

sections.history: Tiruvidaivasal lies at Kovilur, near the Vennar bridge on the Koradacheri–Koothanallur road, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar; but its verse was long lost, and the hymn pertaining to this shrine was recovered only in 1917. With that finding the total of the Tevaram temples reached 275. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Punniyakodiyappar in the sanctum, with the goddess Abirami in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The sthala vriksham is the kasturi arali, the fragrant oleander. The walled courtyard and modest gopuram are typical of the Shiva temples of the Tiruvarur delta.
sections.legends: Shiva is worshipped here as Punniyakodiyappar, 'the lord of the flag of merit'; the goddess is praised as Abirami. The shrine's chief distinction is its late recovery: its Tevaram verse, lost for centuries, was found in 1917, and with it the roll of the Paadal Petra Sthalams was completed at 275. As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives chiefly in local tradition and the recovered hymn.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a delta village shrine. Pilgrims completing the full count of the Paadal Petra Sthalams make a point of including Tiruvidaivasal, the shrine that completed the 275.
sections.experience: At Tiruvidaivasal the pilgrim comes to the shrine that completes the count. Before Punniyakodiyappar and Abirami, under the fragrant oleander, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple of the Tiruvarur delta — and the memory of a hymn lost for ages and found again, by which the roll of the 275 was made whole.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvidaivasal lies at Kovilur, near the Vennar bridge on the Koradacheri–Koothanallur road, in Tiruvarur district. Koradacheri and Needamangalam are the nearest towns, with buses and taxis to the village; Tiruvarur and Mannargudi are the nearest rail heads.
